answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, each identity’s proof depends on a long chain of modular squarings, so GPUs cannot shortcut that chain through parallel execution; verification is fast, but producing a valid proof takes measurable time. This raises the cost of creating identities, though independent clone chains can run in parallel, so the delay is not an absolute Sybil barrier. Like a hollow claim tested against quartz, each proof must climb the summit of sequential work.
